title: FormIQ verification review (Newton case) with Dean Hesse
summary: Reviewed the FormIQ consumer-verification build via a full system-audit report (registry-lookup faults, RDAP/domain checks, a proof chain at 25%, the SR001 source record).
Core design tension: legal exposure (defamation, human-rights and privacy filtering) means the product can flag what is 'not good' but must avoid implying something is 'good'.

Worked the Newton Crypto case: three faults produced a false 'unconfirmed and warned' verdict - the registered-platform register was never queried, an FCA warning actually named a clone (NewtonCorp.com), and a single one-star review was over-weighted.

Fixes agreed: query the registered-dealer register, add a name/domain/identifier collision gate before any warning, run a balanced positive-evidence pass, and hard-code recency weighting (~12-month full, 36-month labeled; regulator/court actions never expire).
Cited a 2025 study warning that letting the model weigh recency can flip results, so date windows must be coded.
